deep.reconstruction:
This page continues E477, Euler's founding paper on double zeta values. In §3 (previous page) Euler set m=n. Here he first notes that among the diagonal series the case n=1 diverges (Δ = harmonic series) and all the others converge.

§4 treats m≠n. In modern notation, Euler's series is
S(m,n) = Σ_{k≥1} k^{-m} Σ_{j≤k} j^{-n} = ζ*(m,n),
with the inner sum non-strict, so it includes the diagonal j=k. He writes this as ∫(1/z^m)(1/y^n), where ∫ denotes summation, and swapping the exponents gives ∫(1/z^n)(1/y^m).

He restates the relation found by his first method:
ζ*(m,n) + ζ*(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n).
The reason: the two series together cover every pair (j,k) once, and the diagonal j=k twice. In strict-sum notation this is ζ(m,n) + ζ(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n), the depth-2 harmonic (stuffle) product.

Euler remarks that neither series can be summed separately by this method. If one becomes known from elsewhere, the other follows. Nothing more can be drawn from the first method, so he moves on.

§5 opens the 'Second Method'. The quantity ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) is the sum over all j≠k of j^{-m}k^{-n}. On the next page Euler splits it into double families of series of the form Σ_x 1/(x^m (x+a)^n), and then decomposes each term into partial fractions (citing the Introductio). This is the route to his explicit evaluations, for example ζ(2,1) = ζ(3) and the formulas for weight m+n odd.
errors: None. The identity is correct with Euler's convention of non-strict inner sums (zeta-star values). The divergence of the case m=n=1 is correctly noted; for m≠n the relation requires both series to converge (e.g. m≥2, n≥1 for the one series, and correspondingly for its partner when n=1).

ideas.what: Notation for double sums Σ k^{-m} Σ_{j≤k} j^{-n} and the symmetric relation S(m,n) + S(n,m) = ζ(m)ζ(n) + ζ(m+n)
ideas.modern_name: Double zeta(-star) values; depth-2 harmonic (stuffle) product / reflection formula
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, and earlier letters to Goldbach of 1742); generalized as the quasi-shuffle algebra by Hoffman (1992, 1997)
ideas.where_published: E477, Novi Comm. Acad. Sci. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera omnia I.15

ideas.what: Reducing ζ(m)ζ(n) − ζ(m+n) to off-diagonal sums Σ 1/(x^m (x+a)^n), to be attacked by partial fractions
ideas.modern_name: Partial-fraction method for Euler sums (cf. Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn 1995)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the well-known stuffle/reflection relation for double zeta values, universally credited to Euler's E477. Nothing on the page is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: None significant; the transcription matches the image. The ∫ symbols denote summation (Euler's long-s summation sign), not integrals.
